$comment: Hatsu's OWN workflow policy. This file is the policy half of the two-file configuration model documented in docs/WORKFLOW.md: nen/contract.json says what nen EXECUTES (lanes, argv, preconditions, hosts, targets), this file says what the workflow DECIDES with (branch shape, which declared verbs run per iteration, the coverage ladder, where reports go, which trailers a commit may carry, which model tier a persona gets). At the pinned nen 0.9.0 `nen schema check` VALIDATES this file -- an `ok nen/workflow.json` row, and a FAIL by pointer on a malformed key -- and two verbs read parts of it: `nen commit format --repo` takes `commits.allowedAttributionTrailers`, and `nen shu coverage --touched` takes the `coverage` ladder when no `--threshold` is given. Everything else here is read by the skills themselves, which is a read rather than a residue: nen validates this file, it does not hand the values out. Every value here is a policy default, not a fact about the machine.

branch.$comment: {model} is the MODEL ALIAS the actor runs on (opus, sonnet, haiku, fable), {persona} the roster persona it acts as, {descriptor} a short kebab noun phrase for the effort. Example: opus/kurapika/machinery-wave-1. `base` is the trunk breath fast-forwards, ao pulls from, and the PreToolUse hook refuses a commit or a push on.

iteration.$comment: The declared verbs the loop runs, three times over, for three different questions -- breath proves them on the branch's fresh tip (was the base sound), rasengan runs them as the author's own inner-loop feedback while it writes the change (does what I just wrote work), and kokusen runs them over the finished tree before every commit and refuses a red one (is the tree I am about to record green). THE COMPILE-BEFORE-COMMIT IS KOKUSEN'S AND RASENGAN IS THE AUTHORING PHASE -- the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-10, docs/ROSTER.md. Hatsu is bash-and-markdown: its general mechanical check is `claude plugin validate . --strict`, declared as the `plugin` lane's `lint`. There is no general test suite; the separate `plugin-bump-guard` lane is a focused fixture used only when scripts/plugin_bump_check.sh changes. It is not an iteration check, full regression, or evidence for unrelated behavior.

tests.$comment: Hatsu ships no general automated test suite, so tsukuyomi has nothing to run here and says so rather than inventing a runner. scripts/plugin_bump_check.sh has a separate focused plugin-bump-guard lane, run only when that executable changes; it does not make this empty required set a passing general regression. An empty `required` is a statement, not an omission.

coverage.$comment: The ladder gyo reports against, in percent line coverage of TOUCHED files. Under `minimum` is a G5 stop, never a lowered bar. Hatsu declares no coverage verb, so gyo reports `not measurable here` against this ladder rather than a number — the ladder still ships because it is the policy every repository Hatsu drives inherits when it declares none of its own.

launch.$comment: Hatsu has no runnable application: it is a plugin read by Claude Code. amaterasu names that fact and launches nothing. A repository with launch targets names them in nen/contract.json under project.launch and selects one here.

reports.$comment: `dir` is git-ignored (.gitignore). `retain: final-only` governs what is KEPT, not whether a working file exists (maintainer's ruling, 2026-09-09): only the final post-merge report gets a dated file of its own under `dir`, and the per-turn and landing reports are published to the conversation as an Artifact -- or, on a surface that cannot publish one, opened from the TRANSIENT `<dir>/current.html`, which every render overwrites and git ignores. One always-latest working file is not a retained report. `template` names templates/<name>.html in this repository.

notifications.$comment: jutaisho's ladder, innermost first: `push` is the surface's own turn-complete signal, `os` an osascript notification, `sound` /System/Library/Sounds/<sound>.aiff through afplay. hooks/stop-bell.sh rings rungs 2 and 3 off .nen/last-stop.json; a rung absent from this list is not rung. `turn` decides how loud an ORDINARY turn is -- one with no gate: `rung1` (the default, and what an absent key reads as) rings only the first rung `rungs` lists, `all` rings every rung it lists. A GATE always rings everything `rungs` lists regardless of `turn`, and `turn` can only WITHHOLD an escalation `rungs` already grants -- it can never conjure a rung `rungs` does not list. nen reads and validates this key from v0.5.0 -- a closed set of `rung1` and `all`, refused by pointer on anything else -- and fires none of the three rungs itself; hooks/stop-bell.sh is what rings them.

commits.$comment: Prospective commits carry exactly the canonical persona/plane key that truthfully identifies the responsible actor: Hatsu-Agent for Hatsu work, Akatsuki-Agent for autonomous Akatsuki work. Do not infer a persona from a runtime alias or default one blindly. Model, surface, runtime, session, and generated-credit attribution remain forbidden in commit messages and bodies. The final PR ledger records actual participants and contributions. Existing commits and dated evidence are historical and are not rewritten.

monitor.$comment: en's izanagi cap and its poll interval. The cap is grammar, not a default: a watch loop with no cap does not run.

models.rule: latest alias only, never a version; subagents never on the frontier tier

cursor.note: Cursor-native only; provider models there are reserved for Bugbot

models.$comment: A tier is named, never a model version — a pinned version is a pin that rots. The orchestrator tier is the main session's; a SUBAGENT never runs on it, because the frontier tier is where the human's own conversation lives and a delegate that outranks its caller has inverted the delegation.
